programs.name: HomeGrown Purchase Assistance
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing
programs.amount: Up to $70,000 toward down payment and closing costs
status: Applications opened June 8, 2026; funds go first come, first served until they run out.
programs.note: The grant depends on income and which zone the home is in (up to 150% of area median income in Zone B), may not exceed 25% of the price, and needs homebuyer counseling, 1% of the price from you and five years living there. Apply through The Resurrection Project or NHS Chicago.

programs.name: Downpayment Plus
programs.by: Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago, through member banks
programs.amount: Up to $10,000, forgiven over time
status: 2026 funding is $48 million; it runs until the money is used.
programs.note: Ask your lender whether it takes part. Downpayment Plus Advantage works the same way through nonprofit mortgage programs.

programs.name: IHDA Access down payment help
programs.by: Illinois Housing Development Authority
programs.amount: $6,000 forgivable, $7,500 deferred, $10,000 repayable, or up to $15,000 for first-time buyers (Access Home)
programs.note: Comes with an IHDA first mortgage. Income and price limits depend on the county and household size; an IHDA lender checks them.

programs.name: Home Repair Program (roofs and porches)
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing
programs.amount: Roof or porch repair, based on an inspection
status: Registration opens once a year for about two weeks (it ran March 10–21, 2025). Next dates are posted on the program page.
programs.note: Registering doesn't guarantee a repair; the city picks from the registrations by need and money available.
remind: Registration has opened in March for about two weeks.

programs.name: Emergency Heating Repair Program
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing
programs.amount: Furnace or boiler repair or replacement in winter
status: Open each winter, first come, first served (last posted window: Nov. 1, 2024 to April 1, 2025).
programs.note: Your name must have been on the deed for at least a year, and utilities must be on. Sell or move out within a year and you repay part of it.
remind: It has opened Nov. 1 each winter.

programs.name: Small Accessible Repairs for Seniors (SARFS)
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing
programs.amount: Free grab bars, railings, door and window fixes, smoke and CO detectors
status: The waiting list closed Dec. 21, 2022; only people already on it are being served.
programs.note: Listed so you know it exists if the list reopens.

programs.name: Homeowner Exemption
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Lowers the taxable value of your home; about $950 a year on average
status: Renews by itself once you have it; missed years can be claimed back.
programs.note: For the home you live in. Check your last bill or the Assessor's site to see if you already get it.
programs.short: About $950 a year off your taxes

programs.name: Senior Exemption
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Lowers the taxable value of your home
status: Renews by itself; missed years can be claimed back.

programs.name: Senior Freeze (Low-Income Senior Assessment Freeze)
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Freezes the taxable value of your home
programs.note: Total household income of $65,000 or less (the Assessor checks the year before the tax year).

programs.name: Persons with Disabilities Exemption
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Lowers the taxable value of your home
status: Renews by itself under a new state law.

programs.name: Veterans with Disabilities Exemption
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Lowers the taxable value of your home; the amount depends on the disability rating

programs.name: Returning Veterans Exemption
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Lowers the taxable value of your home in the year you return
status: File for each year of return from active duty in an armed conflict.

programs.name: Home Improvement Exemption
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Up to $75,000 of added value isn't taxed for four years
programs.note: Good to know before you add a room or a coach house.
programs.short: Up to $75,000 of added value untaxed

programs.name: LIHEAP energy bill help
programs.by: State of Illinois, through CEDA in Cook County
programs.amount: Help with gas and electric bills, reconnection and furnace repair
status: Oct. 1, 2026 to Aug. 13, 2027, or until the money runs out.
programs.note: Renters whose heat is included in rent can get cash help too. CEDA also runs free weatherization for income-eligible homes.
programs.short: Help with heat and power bills

programs.name: Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Family and Support Services
programs.amount: Back rent, future rent or a security deposit to stop an eviction or homelessness
status: The online portal closed March 28 until more money comes in; Community Service Centers can still help by phone or in person.
programs.note: For low-income households at risk of eviction or losing income; open regardless of immigration status.

programs.name: Free weatherization (Illinois Home Weatherization Assistance Program)
programs.by: State of Illinois, through local community action agencies (CEDA in Cook County)
programs.amount: Insulation, air sealing, furnace or water heater repair or replacement: up to $20,000 of energy work and $4,000 of health and safety work a home
programs.note: Households that got LIHEAP in the last 12 months qualify automatically. Renters need the landlord's permission.

programs.name: CHA public housing and project-based voucher waiting lists
programs.by: Chicago Housing Authority
programs.amount: Rent set at about 30% of income in a CHA apartment or a building with CHA vouchers
status: Public housing, project-based voucher and PBRA lists are open; the Housing Choice Voucher list is closed.
programs.note: Joining is free; housing authorities never charge to apply. Waits can be long.

programs.name: Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF)
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development
programs.amount: Up to $150,000 per commercial property ($250,000 with several tenants or for industrial)
status: Opens one TIF district at a time for 30 days; the city announces districts monthly.
src: Department of Planning and Development, April 2026
programs.note: Pays you back after the work for roofs, facades, mechanicals, ADA and similar. Not for homes or home businesses.

programs.name: Neighborhood Opportunity Fund
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development
programs.amount: Up to $250,000, covering 75% of eligible costs
src: Department of Planning and Development, April 2026
programs.note: Only on eligible South, Southwest and West Side commercial corridors (check the city's map). You need to show you can pay half the project. Can pay for buying the property and new buildings on empty lots.

programs.name: Community Development Grant
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development
programs.amount: Small: up to $250,000 (75% of costs). Medium: $300,001 to $5 million. Large: over $5 million
status: Small grants open twice a year (the last round closed Aug. 14, 2026); large grants are rolling.
src: Department of Planning and Development, April 2026
programs.note: Commercial, mixed-use, industrial and community buildings.

programs.name: 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing
programs.amount: Up to $1.8 million a year in credits for 10 years (sold to investors for equity)
status: One competitive round a year under the city's Qualified Allocation Plan, starting with a Preliminary Project Application.
programs.note: Rental homes for households at or below 60% of area median income (average 57% or less with income averaging). The deal check scores your site against the plan.
programs.short: Up to $1.8M a year in credits

programs.name: 4% tax credits with tax-exempt bonds
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing or IHDA
programs.amount: About 4% of qualified basis a year for 10 years, not competitive
status: The city takes bond-only applications on a rolling basis.
src: Nixon Peabody on the 2025 federal tax law
programs.note: For bonds issued after 2025, bonds must pay for at least 25% of the land and building (it was 50%).
programs.short: About 4% of basis a year in credits

programs.name: Multifamily gap financing
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing
programs.amount: Up to 20% of total development cost at the first application
status: Same timeline as the city's tax credit round.
programs.note: Soft loan repaid from 25% of surplus cash. In 2023–24 the city put in $217,504 per home on average, counting all its sources.

programs.name: IHDA 9% tax credits (City of Chicago set-aside)
programs.by: Illinois Housing Development Authority
programs.amount: Up to $1.7 million a year for 10 years; IHDA aims about 12% of its 9% credits at Chicago
status: One round a year under IHDA's plan, with a preliminary application first.
programs.note: A second door besides the city's own credits. Chicago projects must set aside 10% of homes at 30% of area median income for the Statewide Referral Network.
programs.short: Up to $1.7M a year in credits

programs.name: IHDA soft loans (Trust Fund, HOME, National Housing Trust Fund)
programs.by: Illinois Housing Development Authority
programs.amount: In Chicago, up to 10% of total development cost
status: Offered with IHDA's tax credit rounds and its supportive housing requests for applications.
programs.note: Statewide in 2026: Illinois Affordable Housing Trust Fund $55 million, HOME $15.7 million, National Housing Trust Fund $6.7 million (for homes at 30% of area median income). Below-market loans repaid from 25% of surplus cash over at least 30 years.

programs.name: IHDA first mortgage (FHA Risk-Sharing)
programs.by: Illinois Housing Development Authority
programs.amount: Fixed-rate loans of $1 million or more, 17 to 40 years
status: Rates posted by IHDA and given on request.
programs.note: For tax credit and other income-restricted rentals. 1.15 debt coverage (1.11 with rent subsidy), up to 87% of value (90% with subsidy). State prevailing wages apply.

programs.name: FHA 221(d)(4) construction and permanent loan
programs.by: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, through approved lenders
programs.amount: One fixed-rate loan for building and the 40 years after
status: Apply through a HUD-approved lender any time.
programs.note: Quoted at 6.75% to 7.25% on Nov. 11, 2026, plus a 0.25% yearly mortgage insurance premium. Federal Davis-Bacon wages apply.

programs.name: CHA project-based vouchers
programs.by: Chicago Housing Authority
programs.amount: Rent help tied to homes in your building, under 15- to 30-year contracts
status: Competitive; CHA's board approves each development.
programs.note: Tenants pay about 30% of income and CHA pays the rest of the contract rent, which lets the building carry a bigger mortgage. Ask DevelopmentFinancing@theCHA.org.

programs.name: Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund
programs.by: Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund
programs.amount: Yearly rent subsidies for up to 20% of a building's homes, or forgivable money (MAUI) for homes at 30% of area median income
status: Ask the Trust Fund about current funding.
programs.note: For households at or below 30% of area median income. Funded by city fees paid in place of affordable homes, city money and the state Rental Housing Support Program.
programs.short: Rent help for the lowest incomes

programs.name: City housing bond: rental production and Green Social Housing fund
programs.by: City of Chicago
programs.amount: Gap money for 600 to 1,000 affordable rental homes, and low-cost loans for mixed-income buildings that don't use tax credits
status: Awarded through the city's housing funding rounds.
programs.note: Part of the 2024–2028 Housing and Economic Development Bond. Can fund projects outside TIF districts.

programs.name: Affordable Housing Special Assessment Program
programs.by: Cook County Assessor
programs.amount: Lower property taxes for 10 or 30 years on buildings with affordable homes
status: Part 1 before the building opens; apply by Sept. 5 to count for that tax year.
programs.note: Buildings of 7+ homes with 15% or 35% of homes at 60% of area median income or less, after new construction or a big rehab.

programs.name: Illinois Affordable Housing Tax Credit (donations)
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Housing (in Chicago) and IHDA
programs.amount: Donors get a state tax credit worth 50% of what they give the project
status: Applied for with the city's housing funding.
programs.note: For nonprofit sponsors. Rentals: at least 25% of homes at 60% of area median income or less.
programs.short: Donors get 50% back as a state credit

programs.name: Affordable Housing Program (AHP)
programs.by: Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago, with a member bank
programs.amount: Up to $2 million a project
status: One round a year; 2026 applications were due June 12, 2026.
programs.note: Competitive. Apply jointly with a member bank.
remind: FHLBank Chicago opened its 2026 round May 4.

programs.name: Illinois Historic Preservation Tax Credit
programs.by: Illinois State Historic Preservation Office
programs.amount: 25% of rehab costs, up to $3 million a project
status: Two rounds a year; the state hands out $25 million a year.
programs.note: Buildings on the National Register (or in a listed district) that earn income after the rehab. Pairs with the 20% federal historic credit.

programs.name: Opportunity Zone
programs.by: U.S. Treasury (federal tax law)
programs.amount: Investors who put capital gains into new building here can cut their federal taxes
status: The 2018 map runs through 2028; a new map takes effect Jan. 1, 2027.
src: Crowe on the 2025 federal tax law
programs.note: Brings equity, not a grant. Works best with market-rate or mixed-income buildings.

programs.name: Missing Middle Infill Housing Initiative
programs.by: City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development
programs.amount: City lots for $1 plus up to $150,000 a home in construction help
status: Rounds by neighborhood (so far North Lawndale; then Chatham, South Chicago and Morgan Park). Applications go through ChiBlockBuilder.
programs.note: Homes are sold at market prices to people who will live in them.
programs.short: $1 lots plus up to $150,000 a home
